title: Makeopaca
summary: Makeopaca is a Gravesend placename from a July 1684 land transfer, with Moeung marking the eastward end of the beach in the boundary description.
address_label: General Gravesend / Strome Kill area, Brooklyn, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general Gravesend and Coney Island Creek shoreline point based on the 1684 Makeopaca/Moeung boundary description; not an exact deed boundary.
introduction_content: Makeopaca and Moeung belong to the same Gravesend boundary landscape in Brooklyn. Moeung names the eastward end of the beach, while Makeopaca names the larger parcel described from that point.
history_content: Makeopaca connects a Gravesend beach and meadow landscape with a related Native placename. Dated source details appear in the Historic Timeline with their own references.
translation_content:
Moeung is interpreted as a black or miry place, likely referring to meadows at the end of the beach. Makeopaca remains the associated parcel name from the same boundary description.

Why Place Names Matter

“Carrying names forward is a sign of connection, respect. A way to guide people from the past, through today, and into the future.”

— Theresa Pasqual, Reconciling with the past through place and story (2021), interview transcript
land_loss_content: Makeopaca preserves a Gravesend land record in which Indigenous names marked beaches, creeks, and adjoining tracts. Even where the source text is partly truncated, the deed shows how named places structured colonial land transfers in Kings County.
whereintheworld_content: Tooker associates Makeopaca with a beach and meadow in the Gravesend and Coney Island Creek shoreline landscape. Shoreline change, landfill, and development make its exact historic extent uncertain.
